name: Malawi
summary_text: Malawi is dangerous for trans visitors. The Penal Code criminalises same-sex conduct (up to 14 years) AND Human Dignity Trust lists Malawi as criminalising the gender expression of trans people. A moratorium on prosecutions has held since 2014, but in June 2024 the Constitutional Court upheld the ban — a case brought partly by a local trans woman and her Dutch partner — and religious leaders led nationwide anti-LGBT marches in 2023. Discrimination and violence are regular despite the moratorium.

sources.claim_summary: NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying Human Dignity Trust country profile documents Malawi's criminalisation of same-sex activity (up to 14 years with corporal punishment).

sources.title: ‘Dark Day’ in Malawi for Rights of LGBT People | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Jul 2024): 'Dark Day' in Malawi for Rights of LGBT People — the High Court upheld criminalisation, dashing decriminalisation hopes.

Full judgment: Akster and Another v Director of Public Prosecutions and Another (Constitutional Case 2 of 2021) [2024] MWHC 25 (28 June 2024) - the High Court of Malawi upheld Penal Code sections 153(a), 154 and 156 criminalising 'carnal knowledge against the order of nature', attempts and male-on-male gross indecency, dismissing constitutional challenges on equality, privacy, dignity, liberty and fair-trial grounds.

US State Department 2011 Human Rights Report for Malawi: documents the July 2011 protest killings (20 dead), harsh prisons, and 'discrimination against lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender (LGBT) persons'.

sources.title: Malawi: Arrests, Violence against LGBT People | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: HRW (Oct 2018): 'Malawi: Arrests, Violence Against LGBT People' - documents arrests and violence against LGBT Malawians despite the moratorium on arrests under the criminalising laws.

sources.title: Malawi arrests came with threats, assault, extortion
sources.claim_summary: Erasing 76 Crimes (Dec 2015): two men arrested on homosexuality charges suffered house ransacking, assault, threats of being burned alive, extortion by community police, forced stripping, forced medical examinations and HIV/STD tests, and unauthorised distribution of their photos; CEDEP's Gift Trapence: 'how can LGBTI persons access HIV prevention services when the same government then is making arrests against LGBTI?'

sources.title: Malawi: Trying to elude moratorium on anti-gay arrests
sources.claim_summary: Erasing 76 Crimes (April 2018): 'Malawi: Trying to elude moratorium on anti-gay arrests' - police arrested Limbani Sibande (24) in Mzuzu, charging him with 'gross indecency' under Section 156 rather than Section 153, apparently to evade the six-year moratorium while the laws face a constitutional challenge.
